# Block types

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-docs.mts — edit the catalog, not this file. -->

Every block has a name, a summary, a description and a position. What differs is
the `data` payload, which is typed per block type. That payload is what makes a
diagram implementable rather than decorative.

## Interface

### 🖥 `ui_screen` — Screen

A page or screen the user sees.

**When to use it.** One per route or page. Give it the route, the state it holds and the actions the user can take.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `route` | text | URL path, e.g. /checkout. |
| `purpose` | textarea | What the user accomplishes here. |
| `layout` | text | Layout or template this screen uses. |
| `components` | list of strings | Components rendered on this screen. |
| `state` | list of objects | Local state this screen keeps. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `actions` | list of objects | Things the user can do here. |
| ↳ `name` | text | e.g. Submit order. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What happens. |
| ↳ `calls` | text | Block this action calls. |
| `permissions` | list of strings | Roles allowed to open this screen. |

### 🧩 `ui_component` — Component

A reusable piece of interface.

**When to use it.** For anything rendered inside a screen and reused, with props and events.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `purpose` | textarea | What this component is for. |
| `props` | list of objects | Inputs the component accepts. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `emits` | list of objects | Events the component raises. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Event name. |
| ↳ `payload` | text | Data sent with it. |
| ↳ `description` | text | When it fires. |
| `state` | list of objects | Internal state. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `variants` | list of strings | Visual variants, e.g. primary, ghost. |

## Logic

### 🔌 `api_endpoint` — API Endpoint

An HTTP route on the backend.

**When to use it.** One per route. The method, path, request and response shapes are enough to generate the handler.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | one of `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS` | HTTP verb. |
| `path` | text | e.g. /api/orders/:id |
| `auth` | one of `none`, `user`, `admin`, `service` | Who may call this. |
| `summary` | textarea | What the endpoint does. |
| `pathParams` | list of objects | Parameters embedded in the path. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `queryParams` | list of objects | Query-string parameters. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `requestBody` | list of objects | Body fields the client sends. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `responses` | list of objects | Successful responses. |
| ↳ `status` | number | HTTP status code. |
| ↳ `description` | text | When it is returned. |
| ↳ `body` | list of objects | Fields in the response body. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `errors` | list of objects | Failure cases. |
| ↳ `status` | number | HTTP status code. |
| ↳ `code` | text | Application error code. |
| ↳ `when` | text | What triggers it. |
| `notes` | textarea | Anything else the implementer needs. |

### ⚙️ `service` — Service

A module of business logic.

**When to use it.** Group related functions that belong to one responsibility, e.g. PaymentService.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `responsibility` | textarea | The one thing this service owns. |
| `functions` | list of objects | Functions this service exposes. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Function name. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What it does. |
| ↳ `async` | boolean | Returns a promise. |
| ↳ `params` | list of objects | Arguments the function takes. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| ↳ `returns` | text | Return type or value. |
| ↳ `steps` | list of strings | Pseudo-code, one step per line. |
| ↳ `throws` | list of strings | Errors this function can raise. |
| `dependencies` | list of strings | Other services or libraries it needs. |

### ƒ `function` — Function

A single function described as pseudo-code.

**When to use it.** When one routine deserves its own box — the algorithm matters. Write the body as ordered steps.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | text | Optional language hint. |
| `signature` | text | Full signature if you have one. |
| `params` | list of objects | Arguments. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `returns` | text | What it returns. |
| `async` | boolean | Returns a promise. |
| `steps` | list of strings | Pseudo-code, one step per line. |
| `throws` | list of strings | Errors it can raise. |
| `notes` | textarea | Edge cases, performance notes. |

### ⏱ `job` — Job

Background or scheduled work.

**When to use it.** Cron tasks, queue workers, webhook handlers — anything not driven by a user request.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | one of `cron`, `queue`, `webhook`, `manual`, `startup`, `event` | What starts it. |
| `schedule` | text | Cron expression or interval. |
| `steps` | list of strings | What the job does, in order. |
| `idempotent` | boolean | Safe to run twice. |
| `retries` | number | How many times to retry. |
| `notes` | textarea | Timeouts, locking, alerting. |

## Data

### 🗃 `data_model` — Data Model

An entity: a table, collection or type.

**When to use it.** One per persisted entity. Fields and relations here become your schema or migrations.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storage` | text | Where it lives, e.g. postgres. |
| `tableName` | text | Physical name. |
| `fields` | list of objects | Columns or properties. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `relations` | list of objects | Links to other models. |
| ↳ `to` | text | The other model. |
| ↳ `kind` | one of `one-to-one`, `one-to-many`, `many-to-one`, `many-to-many` | Cardinality. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What the link means. |
| `indexes` | list of strings | Indexes to create. |
| `constraints` | list of strings | Uniqueness, checks, cascade rules. |

### 💾 `datastore` — Datastore

A database, cache or bucket.

**When to use it.** To show the infrastructure your models live in, and which entities it holds.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `engine` | text | e.g. PostgreSQL 16, Redis, S3. |
| `purpose` | textarea | What it is used for. |
| `entities` | list of strings | Models stored here. |
| `notes` | textarea | Sizing, retention, backups. |

## Integration

### 🌐 `external_service` — External Service

A third-party API you depend on.

**When to use it.** Stripe, SendGrid, an internal microservice — anything you call but do not build.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | text | e.g. Stripe. |
| `protocol` | one of `http`, `grpc`, `websocket`, `sdk`, `webhook`, `smtp`, `other` | How you talk to it. |
| `operations` | list of objects | Calls you make against it. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Operation name. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What it does. |
| `authMethod` | text | API key, OAuth, mTLS… |
| `envKeys` | list of strings | Environment variables it needs. |

### 📣 `event` — Event

A message published and consumed asynchronously.

**When to use it.** When parts of the system talk without calling each other directly.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel` | text | Topic, queue or channel name. |
| `payload` | list of objects | Fields carried by the event. |
| ↳ `name` | text | Field name. |
| ↳ `type` | text | Type as it will appear in code, e.g. string, number, User[]. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | Must always be present. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What this field holds. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A sample value. |
| `producers` | list of strings | Blocks that emit it. |
| `consumers` | list of strings | Blocks that handle it. |
| `deliveryGuarantee` | one of `at-most-once`, `at-least-once`, `exactly-once`, `unspecified` | Delivery semantics. |

## Flow

### 🔀 `decision` — Decision

A branch in the flow.

**When to use it.** When the path forks. Connect each branch with a conditional edge.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `condition` | textarea | The question being asked. |
| `branches` | list of objects | Possible outcomes. |
| ↳ `label` | text | e.g. yes / no. |
| ↳ `when` | text | Condition for this branch. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What happens next. |

### 🔁 `loop` — Loop

Repeated work.

**When to use it.** When something happens per item or until a condition holds.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `over` | text | Collection being iterated. |
| `condition` | text | Continue while this holds. |
| `body` | list of strings | Steps repeated each iteration. |
| `maxIterations` | text | Safety limit, if any. |

## Meta

### 🔑 `config` — Config

Environment variables and settings.

**When to use it.** Collect the keys the app needs so nothing is missing at run time.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | list of objects | Settings the application reads. |
| ↳ `name` | text | e.g. DATABASE_URL. |
| ↳ `description` | text | What it configures. |
| ↳ `required` | boolean | App will not start without it. |
| ↳ `secret` | boolean | Must never be committed. |
| ↳ `example` | text | A safe sample value. |

### 📝 `note` — Note

A sticky note on the canvas.

**When to use it.** Context, open questions, reminders — anything not part of the system itself.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | textarea | The note. |

### ✳️ `custom` — Custom

Anything the other types do not cover.

**When to use it.** An escape hatch: label the kind yourself and add free key/value details.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kindLabel` | text | What kind of thing this is. |
| `entries` | list of objects | Free-form key/value details. |
| ↳ `key` | text | Detail name. |
| ↳ `value` | text | Detail value. |

## Connection types

Connections are typed too. The validator uses the types to flag wiring that cannot
be right — a data model does not "navigate" to a screen.

| Type | Reads as | Meaning | Usually from | Usually to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `calls` | calls | Source invokes the target and waits for a result. | `service`, `function`, `api_endpoint`, `job`, `ui_screen`, `ui_component` | `service`, `function`, `api_endpoint`, `external_service`, `job` |
| `data_flow` | data | Data moves from source to target. | anything | anything |
| `navigation` | navigates to | The user moves from one screen to another. | `ui_screen`, `ui_component` | `ui_screen` |
| `renders` | renders | A screen or component renders another component. | `ui_screen`, `ui_component` | `ui_component` |
| `reads` | reads | Source reads from a data model or datastore. | `service`, `function`, `api_endpoint`, `job`, `ui_screen`, `ui_component` | `data_model`, `datastore`, `config` |
| `writes` | writes | Source creates, updates or deletes stored data. | `service`, `function`, `api_endpoint`, `job`, `ui_screen`, `ui_component` | `data_model`, `datastore` |
| `emits` | emits | Source publishes an event. | `service`, `function`, `api_endpoint`, `job`, `ui_screen`, `ui_component` | `event` |
| `listens` | listens to | Target consumes an event produced elsewhere. | `event` | `service`, `function`, `job`, `ui_screen`, `ui_component` |
| `depends_on` | depends on | Source needs the target to exist before it can work. | anything | anything |
| `conditional` | if | Flow taken only when the edge condition holds. | `decision`, `loop`, `function`, `service`, `job` | anything |
| `error_flow` | on error | Path taken when the source fails. | anything | anything |
